summary: The outgoing House sent the Hegseth impeachment resolution to committee after Trump backed the defense secretary. Hegseth remains in office. House Republicans chose Jim Jordan to lead their response to the incoming Democratic majority. Senate Republicans kept John Thune. The leadership votes settle who will coordinate Republican opposition in January, when Democrats are projected to control both chambers. Trump publicly favors continued economic and naval pressure on Iran, according to Axios, while Qatar still seeks a deal. In Israel, the new parliament was sworn in while Gadi Eisenkot sought a governing coalition. House Oversight Republicans faulted the Justice Department’s handling of Epstein records, giving incoming investigators specific decisions to examine. News reports attributed a planned prisoner exchange to Russian and Ukrainian negotiators. The available extracts left the terms and timing uncertain. Minneapolis’s data-center zoning vote is due November 12. Several election calls are still outstanding. The review also left open the status of proceedings over Trump’s attempt to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook and the outcome of the Venezuela talks.
scope: Focused November 10–11 review of the Hegseth House vote, Republican leadership and reactions, Iran, Israel, Epstein oversight and pending decisions. Final election calls, the Cook case, Venezuela talks, Nvidia’s inquiry and several implementation checks remain incomplete.
